content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something worth acting on.

Your ≈£2,250/mo free cash looks generous. The deposit needs ≈£830/mo, which is ≈21% of take-home — the goal is sized right for your income. The problem is that ≈£1,850/mo of that free cash is currently unaccounted for. Until that's explained, the goal stays theoretical.

So here's the one move: set up a standing transfer of ≈£300/mo on payday. That's roughly half the drift — sized so it doesn't bite. At that pace, the deposit lands in ≈37 months. Without it, the current trajectory puts you at ≈80 months. That gap is the whole argument.

You called the ≈£1,850/mo drift unsure. That's the right call — and it's exactly what a real month settles. The drift either collapses into real spending categories, or it doesn't. Right now, neither of us knows which.

What checking adds: every ≈ figure gets replaced by a real number, estimate against reality, side by side. And the habits half of the picture is still completely empty — timing, patterns, what's recurring — because estimates can't see it, and only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
